newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Mappin in talks to buy Mesbla - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Mappin in talks to buy Mesbla - paper.

text.p: Brazilian department store chain Mappin, owned by businessman Ricardo Mansur, is negotiating to buy a controlling stake in ailing retailer Mesbla, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper today said.
The paper said local investment bank Banco Pactual, which has been managing Mesbla, is also holding talks with U.S. and Dutch investors to sell the retailer.
"Ricardo and I already had some 10 meetings, but we are not close to a deal yet," Jose Paulo Ferraz do Amaral, an executive at Banco Pactual managing the company, was quoted as saying.

"In addition, I will go to the United States Wednesday to meet executives at a large retail chain and an investment bank representing two U.S. retailers and one Dutch retail chain, which want to hear about Mesbla," Amaral told the paper.
No Pactual officials were immediately available for comment on the report, while a spokesman for Mansur said he would not comment on the issue.

Once a leading local retailer, Mesbla filed for debt relief under a section of the bankruptcy law equivalent to Chapter 11 in the U.S. in August 1995 due to a massive debt reportedly now at about 900 million reais.
Banco Pactual took over management of Mesbla late last year as part of a plan to restructure the firm's debt.
Since Pactual began to administer Mesbla and seek a solution for the company, the market has speculated about potential buyers for the retailer.
Mappin's Mansur acquired control of Casa Anglo, the holding company for Mappin department store, in August 1996 and has been seen as the most likely candidate to assume control of Mesbla.
Mansur is also owner of Brazilian dairy firms Vigor, Leco and Flor da Nata and local bank Banco Crefisul.
